newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle close near highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle close near highs.

text.p: Live and feeder cattle closed higher, although profit-taking pared gains, as fund buying and support from weather concerns continued to support CME live cattle futures with feeder cattle following, traders said.

Fund buying developed when futures showed early strength from concern over cold weather forecasts. The forecast for bitter cold weather to move into most of the U.S. midsection supported February and April live cattle futures, traders said.
Expectations that the cash beef market may be nearing a bottom also lent support.
"I think beef (prices) should bottom this week," one trader with cash connections said.
Boxed values have fallen recently with values down to $104.02 per cwt for lightweight and $103.05 for heavyweight choice beef at noon Monday, the lowest prices since the first week of September.
Cargill Investor Services sold February early before buying by Refco, ADM Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien turned prices higher. Late profit taking kept prices under day's highs, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commercials and commission houses sold the April 66 straddle and 64/66 strangle. There was also scattered selling of February 66 and 68 calls. Volatility was easier on the call selling, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle retained support on spillover demand from live cattle. The large advance in the latest CME feeder cattle index had been expected and provided little direction. Low auction market numbers during the holiday period influenced the index, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $1.67 at $66.04 per cwt.

Spreaders accounted for the bulk of trade late. Cargill Investor Services spread long October feeders/short February live cattle and long August live cattle/short March feeders. There was mixed spreading of long March/short January feeders, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.350 to 0.050 higher with February up 0.325300 at 65.350 cents. Feeder cattle ended up 0.225 to unchanged with March up most at 68.125 cents.
